newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes continue lower, buyers fade.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes continue lower, buyers fade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices continued yesterday's decline in early Friday discussion, tracking a drop in West Texas Intermediate, as local spot trade faded ahead of the weekend, traders said.
Buyers were sidelined after three deals tightened the discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude this week.
"It's a surprising amount," a dealer said, adding he thought fewer deals would be done with several local refiners going into turnaround during January.
Meanwhile, ANS prices fell 15 cents to $24.52/24.72, with the discount stuck at $1.53 under February WTI.
Alyeska, operator of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System, said Thursday a loaded ship weighing more than 150,000 dead-weight tonnes could not leave Alaska's Port of Valdez, until high winds abated.
"We're still making our delivery windows," said a trader for a key Alaskan producer.

A cargo of San Joaquin Valley heavy crude was bought earlier this week at 15 cents below postings, and traders saw the next deal getting done around 25 under, with supply ample as refineries head into turnaround season.
